At time $t$ seconds, $t \geqslant 0$, a particle $P$ has position vector $\mathbf{r}$ metres with respect to a fixed origin $O$, where
$\mathbf{r} = (t^3-8t)\mathbf{i}+\left(\frac{1}{3}t^3-t^2+2t\right)\mathbf{j}$

parts.label: a
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Use of $\mathbf{v}=\frac{d\mathbf{r}}{dt}$ Powers going down by 1. At least 2 powers going down.
A1: $\mathbf{v}=(3t^2-8)\mathbf{i}+(t^2-2t+2)\mathbf{j}$ Any equivalent form
M1: Use of $\mathbf{a}=\frac{d\mathbf{v}}{dt}$ Powers going down by 1. At least 2 powers going down.
A1: $\mathbf{a}=6t\mathbf{i}+(2t-2)\mathbf{j}$ Any equivalent form
A1: $=24\mathbf{i}+6\mathbf{j}\,(\mathrm{m\,s}^{-2})$ Must see acceleration stated as a correct simplified vector. ISW
Official notes (completeness pass):
- Allow column vectors.

parts.label: b
parts.text:
At time $T$ seconds, $T \geqslant 0$, $P$ is moving in the direction of $(2\mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j})$

(b) Find the value of $T$
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Direction $2\mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j}$ Form equation in $t$ or $T$ only using direction. Condone use of 2 on the wrong side. Using their $\mathbf{v}$
A1ft: $(3T^2-8)=2(T^2-2T+2)$ $(T^2+4T-12=0)$ Correct unsimplified equation in $t$ or $T$. Solving not required for the M1. Follow their $\mathbf{v}$: $i$ component $=2(j$ component$)$
A1: $T=2$ Only. Do not need to see method of solution.

questions.stem:
Figure 2

A uniform rod $AB$ has length 4 m and weight 50 N.
The rod has its end $A$ on rough horizontal ground. The rod is held in equilibrium at an angle $\alpha$ to the ground by a light inextensible cable attached to the rod at $B$, as shown in Figure 2. The cable and the rod lie in the same vertical plane and the cable is perpendicular to the rod. The tension in the cable is $T$ newtons.

Given that $\sin\alpha = \frac{3}{5}$

parts.label: a
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Moments about $A$ Dimensionally correct equation i.e. force $\times$ distance = force $\times$ distance. Condone sin/cos confusion. Mark $50g$ as an accuracy error
A1: $4T=2\cos\alpha \times 50$ $(=2\times\frac{4}{5}\times 50)$ Correct unsimplified equation. Need to see $\cos\alpha$ OR $\frac{4}{5}$. Might see LHS $= T\cos\alpha\times 4\cos\alpha+T\sin\alpha\times 4\sin\alpha$
A1*: $T=20$ Obtain given answer from correct working. Must see $\frac{4}{5}$ used correctly.

parts.label: b
parts.text:
Given also that the rod is in limiting equilibrium,

(b) find the value of the coefficient of friction between the rod and the ground.
(6)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Resolve horizontally Condone sin/cos confusion
A1: $H=T\sin\alpha$ Correct equation
M1: Resolve vertically Need all 3 terms. Condone sign error and sin/cos confusion.
A1: $T\cos\alpha+V=50$ Correct equation
Either or both of the above equations could be replaced by a moments equation e.g. $M(B):4\cos\alpha\times V=4\sin\alpha\times H+2\cos\alpha\times 50$ or by resolving perpendicular & parallel to the rod: $T+V\cos\alpha=50\cos\alpha+H\sin\alpha$ & $50\sin\alpha=H\cos\alpha+V\sin\alpha$
M1: Use $F=\mu R$ to form an equation in $\mu$ $(H=\mu V)$ Used, not just stated i.e. they must get as far as substituting their values.
A1: $\mu=\frac{6}{17}$ $\mu=0.35$ or better Accept $\frac{12}{34}$
